documents.title: Private question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is a little embarrassing to ask. For a few months now I have trouble keeping an erection. It used to be fine. Is this a diabetes thing? Could I see a urologist about it? I'd rather not go over it at my regular appointment if that's ok. Thanks, Gary

documents.title: RE: Private question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not embarrassing at all, Gary, and thank you for asking. Yes, diabetes is one of the most common reasons, through its effect on blood vessels and nerves, which you already know about from your feet. I've placed a referral to urology; their office will call you to schedule. If you notice any chest pain or shortness of breath with exertion in the meantime, please tell me right away, since the same blood vessel changes can affect the heart.

conditions.label: Erectile dysfunction
conditions.note: organic, secondary to diabetes, per urology 08/03/2022

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth about 1 hour before sexual activity as needed; no more than once daily

documents.title: Urology consultation (visit 08/03/2022)
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY ASSOCIATES
New patient consultation - 08/03/2022
Re: Gary Kowalczyk, 61 M

Referred for: erectile dysfunction.

HPI: Six months of difficulty maintaining erections sufficient for intercourse. Onset gradual. No penile curvature or pain. Has type 2 diabetes with peripheral neuropathy. No pelvic surgery or trauma.

Medications (as reported): metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. No OTC medications or supplements.
Allergies: ACE inhibitor (cough).
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.
ROS: denies chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath.

Exam: BP 138/86, pulse 78. Otherwise unremarkable, including genitourinary exam. Pedal pulses decreased bilaterally.

Data: Most recent hemoglobin A1c 7.2% (PCP records).

Impression: Organic erectile dysfunction secondary to diabetes mellitus (vascular and neuropathic contribution likely).

Plan:
- Sildenafil 50 mg by mouth about one hour before sexual activity as needed, no more than once in 24 hours. May increase to 100 mg if inadequate response; discussed side effects (headache, flushing, nasal congestion, visual tinge).
- Do not take with any nitrate medication (nitroglycerin, isosorbide). Seek care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours.
- Continue diabetes and vascular risk management with PCP.
- Follow up in urology as needed.

Thank you for the referral.
Urology

documents.title: Annual DM visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SUBJECTIVE: Saw urology 8/3 for ED; started sildenafil 50 prn, using it occasionally, works. Diet and walking continue; weight 89.8 kg (was 95.0 a year ago). Feet numb, stable, no wounds. No exertional symptoms, no claudication. Flu and bivalent COVID 10/20.
Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 20, aspirin 81, sildenafil 50 prn (urology). Urology letter lists lisinopril - not taking since 6/2020 (ACE-I cough).

OBJECTIVE: BP 139/79, HR 66, SpO2 96%.
Gen: well. CV: regular rhythm, no murmur. Resp: clear. Ext: no edema.
Foot exam: skin dry, small metatarsal calluses, no ulcer or maceration; monofilament diminished both feet; DP/PT diminished bilaterally.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. T2DM with CKD 1 and polyneuropathy - annual A1c, CMP, UACR today.
2. HTN - amlodipine 5.
3. Hyperlipidemia - lipids today, atorvastatin 20.
4. PAD, mild - stable.
5. ED - sildenafil per urology. Reminded: never with nitrates.
6. Obesity - BMI now below 30; continue.

RTC 4-5 months.
